ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If the conducting rod ab on the metal rails moves leftward along the rails in a uniform magnetic field, to make an induced current be produced in the copper coil c and make it be attracted by the solenoid, what motion should the conducting rod make?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure there are two horizontal metal rails, and the vertical conducting rod ab bridges across the rails, with a at the upper end and b at the lower end; the region where the conducting rod is located is drawn with a dot array, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. The left side of the rails is connected to a solenoid, and the solenoid, the rails, and the conducting rod form a closed circuit. To the left of the solenoid there is an independent copper coil c; in the figure coil c is close to the solenoid and is not directly connected to the rail circuit. Reasoning: When conducting rod ab moves along the rails in the magnetic field, it produces motional electromotive force, whose magnitude is proportional to speed v, namely ε=BLv, so the magnitude of the current in the solenoid also changes with the rod speed v. To make an induced current be produced in the copper coil c, the magnetic flux through c must change, therefore the solenoid current cannot be constant, and the conducting rod cannot make uniform motion. For coil c to be attracted by the solenoid, according to Lenz's law, it corresponds to the magnetic field produced by the solenoid weakening: when the solenoid current decreases, the induced current in c is in the same direction as the solenoid magnetic field in order to hinder the decrease of magnetic flux, appearing as mutual attraction. Since the magnitude of the solenoid current is proportional to the magnitude of the conducting rod's speed, a decrease in solenoid current requires the conducting rod speed to decrease. Therefore when the conducting rod moves leftward along the rails, it should make decelerated motion.
